### Council

**Three strong models from three model vendors review the work, and you keep scope tight.** Run it when the user says "council", or when a playbook's step calls for one. When the user asked only for a review or advice, run it in review-only mode: edit nothing, run one round, and report.

1. **Get the work ready.** Before an audit, address outstanding PR comments, fix known issues, and run relevant checks. Give council the updated implementation. Do not defer known fixes until reviews return. If the user wants to discard the implementation and explore new ideas, skip fixes to code being replaced. In review-only mode, skip this step.
2. **Pick the members.** Bring in three delegates, usually for review or feedback. Use one strong model from each of three different model vendors, at high reasoning effort or the closest the model offers. A model's vendor is the family that made it, not the provider that runs it. A provider that hosts other vendors' models counts as the vendor of the model it runs, and two accounts of one vendor count once. If the user's instructions name council members, use those. Otherwise use the `council` line in `~/.config/astack/models.md` when it has one. Otherwise pick the latest flagship from each vendor, found in the harness's model list.
3. **Check, then start them in parallel.** Before launch, confirm three seats on three vendors, each at high effort or the closest. In T3 Code, call `orchestrator_capabilities` and confirm each seat's provider instance has `canRunChildTask` true. A seat on a provider other than your own instance also needs `canRunCrossProviderChildTask` true. Then start one `delegate_task` per seat, all in the same turn, with `role: "review"` and `isolation: "shared"`, even when a seat runs on your own vendor ([t3-code.md](../references/harnesses/t3-code.md#panels-and-councils)). Elsewhere, use the harness's subagent tool ([harness references](../references/harnesses/README.md)). Where the harness offers a read-only snapshot or sandbox for a seat, use it. Before launch, save a manifest of the checkout with [`scripts/checkout-manifest.sh`](../scripts/checkout-manifest.sh)` save <scratch>/manifest.txt`, with `<scratch>` outside the checkout. It records each file's checksum and each symlink's target, skipping `.git`, so it catches another edit to a file that was already modified or untracked, which `git status` misses. If you cannot reach three vendors, or a named member is unavailable, report it instead of substituting.
4. **Brief them the same way.** Write each delegate's brief yourself, without the `worker.md` first line. Give it the request and relevant context: the goal, the base and head commits, the files in scope, and what is out of scope. Every brief forbids creating, moving, editing, or deleting any file in the checkout, and sends any scratch output to a folder outside it. Some harnesses don't enforce a review role as read-only, so the brief is the guard. Ask each delegate to name its model and vendor in its first line, then give a score out of 10 and findings with a file, a line, a severity (blocker, major, or minor), and a concrete failure.
5. **Don't wait idle.** When a result arrives, check the model it actually ran on in its status. In T3 Code that is `task_status`'s `executedModel`, which can be missing or null. When it is, the seat's own first line is the only other evidence; the requested model alone is not. Infer the vendor from the model id or label, since the catalog doesn't name it. Count the seat's score only when both the model it ran on and that model's vendor are known, and say which source you used. Otherwise mark the seat unverified. If the seat is unverified, or a requested model or vendor did not run, report it and record the round as incomplete. Do not count a substitute as that seat. After each seat returns, run `checkout-manifest.sh compare <scratch>/manifest.txt`. It exits 1 and lists each stray write, leaving out caches such as `__pycache__`. Report each one with the seats that were running then. Then check its findings against the code at once and decide what to fix while the other delegates run. Do not edit files while a delegate still reviews the same checkout. If the user's instructions mark a delegate as non-blocking, do not wait for it. Treat a late result as feedback and do not record its score.
6. **Summarize.** Collect their responses and summarize the useful findings, disagreements, and recommended next steps. Agreement across vendors is strong evidence. A finding only one member raised needs your own check before you act on it.
7. **Fix and go again.** In review-only mode, stop after the first round. Otherwise, if you agree with their recommendations, make the changes and request a fresh review after. Each fresh review is a new set of delegates with the brief, the earlier findings, and your responses. Count each full review pass as one round. A fresh review after fixes starts a new round. Stop when every delegate scores 8 or more (an unverified seat's score doesn't count), or when a round surfaces no new verified in-scope blocker or major finding. Never run more than 3 rounds. Then report the scores for each round and any disagreement still open.
8. **Hold the scope.** Do not let repeated reviews result in scope creep. It is your job to fight to keep scope limited. A finding outside the request goes in the summary as a follow-up, not into this change, and never blocks.
9. **Record the result.** If the work ends in a pull request, put the results in the PR description in this section:

   ```markdown
   ## Council review

   Rounds: 2

   | Delegate | Round 1 | Round 2 |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | <seat 1 model> | 7/10 | 9/10 |
   | <seat 2 model> | 8/10 | 10/10 |
   | <seat 3 model> | 7/10 | 9/10 |
   ```

   If a delegate gives no score, write `no score`. Do not invent one. Mark an incomplete round `incomplete` and say which seat was missing, substituted, or unverified. If the PR is open, edit the description. Do not post a comment for this. If there is no PR, put the same results in the final reply only.

**Reply:** the members and the models they ran on, the rounds with each score, any incomplete round and unverified seat, any stray write, what you fixed, what you declined and why, any disagreement still open, and any member you could not reach.
